title: What is it like to remember every day of your life? With Michael Yassa, PhD, and Markie Pasternak

sentences.en: Do you remember where you were on April 10th, 1999?
sentences.zh: 你还记得1999年4月10日那天你在哪里吗？

sentences.en: What day of the week was it?
sentences.zh: 那天是星期几？

sentences.en: What about the weather?
sentences.zh: 天气怎么样？

sentences.en: What were you wearing and what did you do all day?
sentences.zh: 你当时穿了什么，一整天都做了些什么？

sentences.en: Chances are you can't answer any of those questions.
sentences.zh: 你很可能回答不上来这些问题中的任何一个。

sentences.en: For most of us, our autobiographical memory is a bit of a blur.
sentences.zh: 对于我们大多数人来说，我们的自传体记忆都有点模糊不清。

sentences.en: Sure, some special occasions stand out, weddings, birthdays, vacations, along with a bundle of random memories that stick with us for no special reason.
sentences.zh: 当然，一些特殊的场合会让人印象深刻，比如婚礼、生日、假期，还有一些毫无缘由却一直留在我们脑海里的零碎记忆。

sentences.en: But for people with highly superior autobiographical memory, or HSAM, every day is memorable.
sentences.zh: 但对于拥有“超强自传体记忆”（HSAM）的人来说，每一天都是值得铭记的。

sentences.en: Ask someone with HSAM what they were doing on April 10th, 1999, or the 11th or the 16th, and they'll be able to tell you, along with a bunch of other checkable facts.
sentences.zh: 问问拥有HSAM的人1999年4月10日，或者11日、16日那天他们在做什么，他们不仅能告诉你，还能提供一堆其他可以核实的事实。

sentences.en: How do they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: How do the brains of people with HSAM store and retrieve this vast amount of detailed autobiographical information?
sentences.zh: 拥有HSAM的人的大脑是如何存储和提取如此海量的详细自传体信息的？

sentences.en: What's it like to be able to remember every day of your life?
sentences.zh: 能够记住生命中的每一天是一种什么样的体验？

sentences.en: Is it a blessing or a curse?
sentences.zh: 这是一种恩赐还是一种诅咒？

sentences.en: And what can studying this unusual ability teach us about how memory works for the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 研究这种非凡的能力又能让我们了解普通人的记忆是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们有两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: Dr. Michael Yassa is the director of the Center for the Neurobiology of Learning and Memory at the University of California, Irvine.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·亚萨博士是加州大学欧文分校学习与记忆神经生物学中心的主任。

sentences.en: The center was established in 1983 by Dr. James McGaw, and it's where the first research on highly superior autobiographical memory began about 15 years ago.
sentences.zh: 该中心由詹姆斯·麦高博士于1983年建立，大约15年前，关于超强自传体记忆的首次研究就是在这里开始的。

sentences.en: Today, Dr. Yassa and his colleagues continue to study HSAM, along with how we learn and remember information, how learning and memory change with age,
sentences.zh: 今天，亚萨博士和他的同事们继续研究HSAM，以及我们如何学习和记忆信息，学习和记忆如何随年龄增长而变化，

sentences.en: and how to better diagnose and treat disorders like Alzheimer's disease.
sentences.zh: 以及如何更好地诊断和治疗阿尔茨海默病等疾病。

sentences.en: Our second guest is Markey Pasternak, one of the few people in the world confirmed to have HSAM.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是马基·帕斯特纳克，她是世界上为数不多被证实拥有HSAM的人之一。

sentences.en: In 2014, when she was a junior in college,
sentences.zh: 2014年，当她还是大学三年级学生时，

sentences.en: Ms. Pasternak learned about highly superior autobiographical memory in one of her psychology courses, realized that it described her special memory,
sentences.zh: 帕斯特纳克女士在一门心理学课程中了解到了超强自传体记忆，意识到这正是她那种特殊记忆的写照，

sentences.en: and began participating in research at UC Irvine.
sentences.zh: 并开始参与加州大学欧文分校的研究。

sentences.en: She went on to earn a master's degree in education, and today works in student affairs at Auburn University, doing mental wellness and health education outreach.
sentences.zh: 后来她获得了教育学硕士学位，目前在奥本大学的学生事务部门工作，负责心理健康和健康教育的推广工作。

sentences.en: She also blogs and speaks to the media about living with HSAM.
sentences.zh: 她还通过博客和媒体分享自己与HSAM共处的生活。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天能参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: Yes, thank you so much for having us.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常感谢你们邀请我们。

sentences.en: Dr. Yassa, you get the first questions.
sentences.zh: 亚萨博士，第一个问题问您。

sentences.en: When people with HSAM retrieve autobiographical memories, are they doing the same thing that most of us do when we remember our past,
sentences.zh: 当拥有HSAM的人提取自传体记忆时，他们所做的事情和我们大多数人回忆过去时是一样的吗，

sentences.en: but they're just much better at it than the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 只是他们比我们其他人做得好得多？

sentences.en: You know, you started with a very difficult question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你一开始就问了一个非常困难的问题，金。

sentences.en: I think this is really what we're trying to get to the bottom of.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是我们试图弄清楚的根本所在。

sentences.en: And part of the problem is that when we were first kind of exposed to this phenomenon, it violated all of our assumptions about how memory works.
sentences.zh: 问题的一部分在于，当我们最初接触到这种现象时，它颠覆了我们关于记忆运作方式的所有假设。

sentences.en: So one of the first thoughts was, well, they must be using a different mechanism.
sentences.zh: 所以最初的想法之一是，嗯，他们一定使用了不同的机制。

sentences.en: But pushed to the extreme, one can imagine that, you know, our regular memory systems just have a degree of variation in them,
sentences.zh: 但推向极致的话，人们可以想象，你知道，我们普通的记忆系统本身就存在一定程度的差异，

sentences.en: that it could be part of the regular mechanisms, just like I said, pushed to the extreme.
sentences.zh: 这可能是常规机制的一部分，就像我说的，被推向了极致。

sentences.en: And we're still not sure if they're part of that natural variation or if they're using very distinct mechanisMs.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然不确定他们是这种自然变异的一部分，还是在使用非常独特的机制。

sentences.en: And that's what we're hoping to uncover in the coming years with some brain imaging techniques and various other methods that look deep into the neurobiology of the brain.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们希望在未来几年通过一些脑成像技术和各种其他深入观察大脑神经生物学的方法来揭示的内容。

sentences.en: Marky, can you talk about how this works for you?
sentences.zh: 马基，你能谈谈这对你来说是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: When you remember a particular day from 10 years ago, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 当你回忆起10年前的某一天时，你在做什么？

sentences.en: Does the memory just pop up or do you have to work to retrieve it?
sentences.zh: 记忆是自动浮现的，还是你需要努力去提取它？

sentences.en: So it kind of depends on the day.
sentences.zh: 这有点取决于具体是哪一天。

sentences.en: I was actually talking to a psychology professor at Auburn about this about a year ago because it's fun working at universities, right?
sentences.zh: 大约一年前，我实际上和奥本大学的一位心理学教授谈过这个问题，因为在大学工作很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the psychology departments get real excited.
sentences.zh: 因为心理学系的人总是特别兴奋。

sentences.en: And what I told him is I, and we kind of coined them,
sentences.zh: 我告诉他，而且我们还给它们起了个名字，

sentences.en: I have these things called go-to dates, right?
sentences.zh: 我有这些所谓的“首选日期”，对吧？

sentences.en: Dates that just stick in my memory because of an event that happened that maybe had more of an emotional connection to it.
sentences.zh: 那些因为发生过某种可能带有更多情感联系的事件而深深印在我记忆中的日期。

sentences.en: So for example, I know like sad example to start off with, but if you ask me the day my father died, right?
sentences.zh: 举个例子，虽然这是一个悲伤的开头，但如果你问我父亲去世的那天，对吧？

sentences.en: I'd be like March 16th, 2014, and most people could probably do that.
sentences.zh: 我会说是2014年3月16日，大多数人可能也能做到这一点。

sentences.en: But then I also can remember, you know, the day I saw a boy I had a crush on in seventh grade for the first time in a while, and that was June 26th, 2007.
sentences.zh: 但我还能记住，你知道，我第一次见到我在七年级暗恋的那个男孩的那天，那是2007年6月26日。

sentences.en: It was a Tuesday, and I could tell you all about that, right?
sentences.zh: 那天是星期二，我可以告诉你关于那天的一切，对吧？

sentences.en: So like they can get, you have more random days that you hold with these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你会因为这些事情而记住更多随机的日子。

sentences.en: But, you know, if I can go real back to, let's say go to that 2007 date, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果我可以回到过去，比如说回到2007年的那个日期，对吧？

sentences.en: If I can go back and say, yeah, I saw this guy, you know, at the ice rink because I was a figure skater, and he was a hockey player,
sentences.zh: 如果我能回到过去说，是的，我在溜冰场看到了这个家伙，因为我以前是个花样滑冰运动员，而他是冰球运动员，

sentences.en: and I like bumped into him there, and I can tell you all about that.
sentences.zh: 我在那里撞见了他，我可以告诉你关于那件事的一切。

sentences.en: I can also piece around the days around it, and that's where the memory kind of starts coming into fruition.
sentences.zh: 我还可以拼凑出那几天前后的事情，这就是记忆开始变得清晰的地方。

sentences.en: And so I can say, oh, I went to that ice skating practice that day, even though I didn't usually skate on Tuesday nights over the summer,
sentences.zh: 所以我可以说，哦，那天我去参加了滑冰训练，尽管我通常夏天晚上不去滑冰，

sentences.en: because I had stayed with another friend on my figure skating team that day, and it was her birthday in a couple days.
sentences.zh: 因为那天我和花样滑冰队的另一个朋友待在一起，过几天就是她的生日了。

sentences.en: And so I was spending time with her because it had just been her birthday party the day before.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时在陪她，因为前一天刚办过她的生日派对。

sentences.en: So I can like that context kind of comes in, and I can start piecing around it.
sentences.zh: 所以那种情境感就出来了，我可以开始拼凑周围的事情。

sentences.en: So sometimes if you ask me like a date, I might be like, oh, wait, I don't know exactly what I did on that day quite yet,
sentences.zh: 所以有时候如果你问我一个日期，我可能会说，哦，等等，我还不确定那天具体做了什么，

sentences.en: but I can go to my nearest go-to date, put the context together, and kind of crawl to it.
sentences.zh: 但我可以去我最近的“首选日期”，把情境拼凑起来，然后慢慢回想起来。

sentences.en: And it's like a mental image for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就像是一幅心理图像。

sentences.en: And I know this is different between different people with HSAM.
sentences.zh: 我知道不同HSAM患者之间的情况有所不同。

sentences.en: I know I've talked to some friends with HSAM who say they just picture like a calendar, like a black and white regular calendar.
sentences.zh: 我知道我和一些有HSAM的朋友聊过，他们说他们脑海里看到的就像一个日历，那种黑白普通的日历。

sentences.en: That's not me.
sentences.zh: 我不是那样的。

sentences.en: I have some synesthesia as well.
sentences.zh: 我还有一些联觉。

sentences.en: So for me, what it looks like is it's like a giant like Candyland board sort of a thing, I think of it, or like a giant map or like a road with a journey,
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，它看起来像是一个巨大的“糖果乐园”游戏棋盘，或者像一张巨大的地图，又或者像一条充满旅程的道路，

sentences.en: and it's all different colors, and there's dates everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是不同的颜色，到处都是日期。

sentences.en: And there's like people and images and places.
sentences.zh: 还有人、图像和地点。

sentences.en: And it's like this fun place in my brain I can kind of go to and like hop around in different days.
sentences.zh: 这就像我大脑中一个有趣的地方，我可以去那里，在不同的日子里跳来跳去。

sentences.en: And I can like zoom in on the days and the years and all in the times and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我可以放大查看那些日子、年份、时间等等所有这些东西。

sentences.en: That sounds amazing.
sentences.zh: 听起来太神奇了。

sentences.en: Well, Markie, when did you first realize that your memory was different from that of other people?
sentences.zh: 那么，马基，你是什么时候第一次意识到你的记忆力与其他人不同的？

sentences.en: How old were you?
sentences.zh: 你当时多大？

sentences.en: And what triggered that realization?
sentences.zh: 是什么触发了这种意识？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I'm going to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，说实话。

sentences.en: I feel like sometimes when I answer this question, I feel like it's supposed to be an aha moment, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得有时候当我回答这个问题时，感觉好像应该有一个“顿悟时刻”，对吧？

sentences.en: Like this big, like, oh my gosh, my brain's different.
sentences.zh: 就像那种巨大的、天哪，我的大脑与众不同的感觉。

sentences.en: But the reality is, is that it was just a series of little moments that added to the realization over a lot of years,
sentences.zh: 但现实是，这只是多年来一系列小瞬间累积起来的认识，

sentences.en: because it's so unique and kind of difficult to figure out, especially when it's happening to you as a kid.
sentences.zh: 因为它太独特了，而且很难弄清楚，尤其是当你还是个孩子的时候。

sentences.en: You know, and you don't really have all the vocabulary to describe what's going on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你并没有足够的词汇来描述正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And so the first time I noticed it was different was probably in 2006.
sentences.zh: 所以我第一次注意到它与众不同可能是在2006年。

sentences.en: I was, I had just turned 12 years old.
sentences.zh: 我当时刚满12岁。

sentences.en: And I started realizing I could remember what I was doing a year ago every day.
sentences.zh: 我开始意识到我能记住一年前每一天我在做什么。

sentences.en: Like I was like, oh, it's, you know, May 11th, like a year ago was our band concert.
sentences.zh: 就像我当时想，哦，你知道，5月11日，一年前那天是我们的乐队音乐会。

sentences.en: And then we left for Florida the next day.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天我们就出发去佛罗里达了。

sentences.en: But like no one else really cared to remember that our band concert was a year ago that day.
sentences.zh: 但没有其他人会在意去记住那天是一年前的乐队音乐会。

sentences.en: But for some reason, I just knew.
sentences.zh: 但出于某种原因，我就是知道。

sentences.en: And like, I remember being like, I should check, like, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 我记得当时想，我应该核实一下，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: I should check this out.
sentences.zh: 我应该查证一下。

sentences.en: So I went to the home video and there it was, like, you know, May 11th, 2005.
sentences.zh: 所以我看了家庭录像，果然就在那里，你知道，2005年5月11日。

sentences.en: And I was like, okay, you know.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，你知道。

sentences.en: And so I started realizing it then.
sentences.zh: 于是我从那时开始意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And then as the years went on, I realized I could keep doing it.
sentences.zh: 随着岁月的流逝，我意识到我可以一直这样做。

sentences.en: Like it wasn't just, I had a good memory for 2005, 2006 stuck, 2007 stuck, 2008 stuck.
sentences.zh: 就像不仅仅是我对2005年有很好的记忆，2006年也记得，2007年也记得，2008年也记得。

sentences.en: And so when I was in eighth grade, I really got obsessed with like memories and old pictures and dates and things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以当我在八年级时，我真的沉迷于记忆、旧照片、日期之类的东西。

sentences.en: And it was just becoming something that was kind of crystallizing in my brain more.
sentences.zh: 它开始在我大脑中变得越来越具体。

sentences.en: And I realized that the first like week I could remember was the week of February 9th through the 13th of 2005.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我能记住的第一周是2005年2月9日到13日那一周。

sentences.en: And the ninth was a Wednesday and everything just kind of starts on that Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 9号是星期三，一切都从那个星期三开始。

sentences.en: And then the next days are real vivid.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几天非常生动。

sentences.en: And then like the next week or two is kind of blurry.
sentences.zh: 然后接下来的一两周有点模糊。

sentences.en: But then after that, everything's really vivid.
sentences.zh: 但那之后，一切都非常生动。

sentences.en: And I was like, you know, do I have those dates right?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，你知道，我记得那些日期对吗？

sentences.en: And so I remember I was, I had a figure skating competition as I was talking about figure skating
sentences.zh: 所以我记得我当时，正如我之前提到的，那个周末我在一个叫比弗达姆的地方参加花样滑冰比赛，威斯康星州，或者像我父亲喜欢叫的那样，比弗达恩。

sentences.en: earlier, uh, that weekend in a place called Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, or as my father liked to call it Beaver Darn.
sentences.zh: 呃，我去了地下室，翻遍了我妈妈装旧纪念品和剪贴簿的箱子。

sentences.en: And, uh, and I went in the basement and I dug through like my mom's like totes of, um, like old memorabilia and scrapbooking stuff.
sentences.zh: 我找到了那次比赛的小册子，上面写着2005年2月13日。

sentences.en: And I found the brochure from that competition and it said February 13th, 2005.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，我确实记得没错。

sentences.en: And I was like, all right, I have something here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我小时候对它的认识过程。

sentences.en: So, and that was kind of the realization of it as a kid.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 今天世界上有79亿人口，上下浮动几千人。

sentences.en: There are 7.9 billion people in the world today, give or take a few thousand.
sentences.zh: 亚萨博士，有多少人被证实患有HSAM，你们是如何找到这些人的？

sentences.en: Dr. Yessa, how many people have been confirmed to have HSAM and how do you find these people?
sentences.zh: 嗯，又是一个棘手的问题，金。

sentences.en: Um, another tricky question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 所以，我会给你我们掌握的答案，但，但有一个警告，对吧？

sentences.en: So, uh, I'll give you the answer that we have, but, but there's a caveat, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们已经确定了，呃，人数不到一百，呃，我们在实验室里确定的，

sentences.en: Um, so we have identified, uh, it's, it's smaller than a hundred, um, that we have identified
sentences.zh: 但是，呃，我们也收到了来自世界各地同事的报告，

sentences.en: in the laboratory, but, uh, we are also getting reports from our colleagues actually around
sentences.zh: 在不同的国家，也有人找到他们说，我对过去有这种极其生动的记忆，而且，呃，他们可能没有看过，

sentences.en: the world, um, in different countries of also having individuals kind of come to them and say, I have this extremely vivid, uh, memory of the past and, uh, they may not have seen,
sentences.zh: 你知道，60分钟节目的片段，也没有在书或论文中读到过，只是觉得这很奇怪，但是，但问题确实在于，直到，

sentences.en: you know, a 60 minutes piece or read about it in a, in a book or a paper, but just sort
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，也许马基已经完成了这个练习并真正证实了它，或者有人看过60分钟的片段，或者读过论文，或者在课堂上听说过。

sentences.en: of think it's curious, but, but that's really the issue is that until, um, you know, maybe Markey
sentences.zh: 真的很难将其视为与其他人不同的东西。

sentences.en: has gone through this exercise and really confirmed it, or somebody has seen a piece on 60 minutes or, or read a paper or heard about it in a class.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜实际上外面有很多人拥有这种能力，只是不知道，也没有理由怀疑它有什么特别之处。

sentences.en: or, you know, what was going on in our family last Christmas or, you know, whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 在我意识到我患有超忆症（HSAM）并且有了名字可以称呼它的时候，我父亲已经去世了。

sentences.en: My dad was already passed away by the time that we realized I had HCM and there was a name to call it.
sentences.zh: 所以他在我发现自己患有超忆症（HSAM）的那一年去世了，就在几个月前。

sentences.en: And so he died a year, like the same year I found out I had HCM, so a couple months before.
sentences.zh: 但我们关于我父亲的记忆是，他有一种令人难以置信的记忆数字的能力。

sentences.en: But what we remember about my father is he had an incredible ability to remember numbers.
sentences.zh: 他记得童年时期的地址，童年时期的电话号码，而他根本不再需要这些了。

sentences.en: He had, he knew people's addresses from his childhood, people's phone numbers from his childhood that he didn't need anymore.
sentences.zh: 他背下了我们全家的社会安全号码，你知道，他张口就能说出来。

sentences.en: He had our whole family's social security numbers memorized, you know, that he could just say.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他有那个能力。

sentences.en: And so, you know, he had that.
sentences.zh: 然后我妈妈有那种记忆力。

sentences.en: And then my mom had the memory thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣，对我来说，这些能力是如何结合在一起的，比如对数字的记忆，

sentences.en: So it's kind of interesting how, for me, those kind of combine in like a memorization of numbers
sentences.zh: 或者记住数字的能力，比如日期，然后还有自传式的部分。

sentences.en: or an ability to remember numbers, like dates, and then also the autobiographical part of it as well.
sentences.zh: 我了解到超忆症（HSAM）与一些心理健康状况之间存在联系。

sentences.en: I understand there are some links between HCM and some mental health conditions.
sentences.zh: Marky，你写过关于你的超忆症（HSAM）与强迫症（OCD）之间联系的文章。

sentences.en: Markie, you've written about the connection between your HCM and obsessive compulsive disorder.
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那个吗？

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 好的，可以。

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的觉得我的超忆症（HSAM）和强迫症（OCD）联系非常紧密。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I really feel like my HCM and OCD are pretty heavily linked.
sentences.zh: 这是因为在我被诊断出患有强迫症后的任何时候，人们都会问：你沉迷于什么？

sentences.en: And it's because any time after I got diagnosed with OCD, people would be like, what are you obsessed with?
sentences.zh: 你沉迷于什么？

sentences.en: What are you obsessed with?
sentences.zh: 我老实说我不知道。

sentences.en: And I honestly didn't know.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，我有强迫行为，我觉得我必须做某些事情，而且我有很大的焦虑，

sentences.en: I was just like, I have compulsions and I feel like I have to do things and I have a lot of anxiety
sentences.zh: 我有囤积东西的倾向，你知道，所有这些我都在接受治疗等等。

sentences.en: and I have a tendency to hoard things, you know, all things I've been treated for and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 但后来当我开始处理我的，你知道，超忆症（HSAM）之类的事情时，我意识到我的痴迷是日期，日期和日历，以及我生活中发生的事件。

sentences.en: But then as I started working with my, you know, with HCM and stuff, I realized my obsession was dates, dates and calendars and my own events in my life.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，它在某种程度上帮助了我，但在我年轻的时候，它在很多方面助长了强迫症，

sentences.en: Because, you know, what it kind of helped me do, but it helped the OCD flourish in a lot of ways when I was younger,
sentences.zh: 因为我能准确地记住事情是如何发生的，然后我会创造一个仪式来强化它。

sentences.en: because I could remember exactly how something happened and then I'd create a ritual to reinforce it.
sentences.zh: 所以会发生的情况是，假设我在参加一场我非常紧张的数学考试那天穿了一件特定的衬衫。

sentences.en: So what would happen was, let's say I wore a particular shirt the day I was taking a math test I was really nervous about.
sentences.zh: 因为我的记忆力，我能记住，你知道，那天我做的一切，我穿的衬衫，我早餐吃了什么，你知道，那天我和谁谈过话。

sentences.en: So because of my memory, I could remember, you know, everything I did that day, the shirt I wore, what I ate for breakfast, you know, who I talked to that day.
sentences.zh: 然后我大脑中负责强迫症的部分就会说：

sentences.en: And then the part of my brain that had, you know, was responsible for my OCD would be like,
sentences.zh: 好吧，下次你有数学考试时，如果你想拿A，猜猜你必须和谁谈话？

sentences.en: all right, well, next time you've got a math test, if you want to get an A, guess who you have to talk to?
sentences.zh: 猜猜你早餐必须吃什么？

sentences.en: Guess what you have to eat for breakfast?
sentences.zh: 猜猜你必须穿什么？

sentences.en: Guess what you have to wear?
sentences.zh: 它开始强化这一点。

sentences.en: And it started reinforcing that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我的记忆力在创造许多仪式方面发挥了很大作用，我曾长期受其奴役。

sentences.en: So I think my memory played a large role into creating a lot of rituals that I was kind of slave to for a long, long time.
sentences.zh: Yassa博士，这在你共事的人群中常见吗？

sentences.en: Dr. Yes, is that common among the people you work with?
sentences.zh: 绝对常见。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到了这些元素，也许在强迫症的全面诊断水平上可能没有那么高，

sentences.en: So we see elements of this, perhaps maybe not at the level of a full diagnosis of obsessive compulsive disorder,
sentences.zh: 但肯定有强迫倾向和痴迷，也就是思想本身。

sentences.en: but certainly obsessive tendencies and obsessions, so the thoughts themselves.
sentences.zh: 这在超忆症（HSAM）群体中似乎表现得更为突出。

sentences.en: That seems to be much more highly represented in the group with H-SAM.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，听Marky谈论这件事对我来说确实很有趣，因为我们一直在努力理解因果链。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's interesting, actually, for me, really, to hear Marquis speak about it, because we've struggled to try to understand the causality chain.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这两者是某种共存的状况，它们在某些个体中相互助长，可能在某种程度上，但在其他人身上则不然？

sentences.en: In other words, is it that those two are sort of co-occurring conditions, and they're sort of feeding off of one another in some individuals, maybe to an extent, but not others?
sentences.zh: 还是其中一个实际上导致了另一个？

sentences.en: Or is one actually leading to the other?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果有与日期相关的痴迷证据，

sentences.en: In other words, if there's evidence of obsessions that are related to dates,
sentences.zh: 如果这发生在任何其他方面可能，你知道，完全正常的人身上，

sentences.en: if that happens in any individual who might otherwise be, you know, perfectly fine,
sentences.zh: 它会导致这种超忆症（HSAM）状况吗？

sentences.en: does it lead to this H-SAM condition?
sentences.zh: 我们不知道答案。

sentences.en: And we don't know the answer to that.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不知道它是否会那么简单或直接。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's going to be that simple or straightforward, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为存在一些有趣的共同特征和共同机制，特别是正如Marky所说，对日期的痴迷，

sentences.en: I do think that there are some interesting shared traits and shared mechanisms, especially, as Marquis was talking about, obsessing over dates,
sentences.zh: 它们变得更加重要，更加有后果，因为你看到了价值。

sentences.en: and they become much more important, much more consequential, because you see the value.
sentences.zh: 那种前馈循环可以促成这种情况，可能导致更高水平的焦虑

sentences.en: That kind of feed-forward cycle can precipitate the condition, can perhaps lead to higher levels of anxiety
sentences.zh: 和更高水平的强迫症，但也可能使超忆症（HSAM）的能力更容易被强化。

sentences.en: and higher levels of OCD, but also can make the H-SAM abilities much more reinforceable.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你经常练习这个并经常思考它，你可以想象，就像任何其他事情一样，你会变得更擅长它。

sentences.en: So if you're practicing this often and thinking about it often, you can imagine, just like anything else, you're going to get better at it.
sentences.zh: Marky之前提到的有一件事，我很喜欢，因为我现在已经从我们的许多志愿者那里听到了，那就是回溯一年的概念。

sentences.en: One thing that Marquis mentioned earlier, which I love because I've heard it now from a number of our volunteers, is the notion of going back a year.
sentences.zh: 所以说，你知道，今天是4月16日。

sentences.en: So saying, you know, today is April 16th.
sentences.zh: 2020年4月16日发生了什么？

sentences.en: What happened on April 16th, 2020?
What about 2019?
What about 2018?
sentences.zh: 我们经常听到这种情况，这看起来，你知道，可能有点奇怪，但它是一种存档机制。

sentences.en: And we will often hear that, and it seems like, you know, kind of a strange thing maybe, but it is an archival mechanism.
sentences.zh: 这是一种日复一日地建立过去记录的方法。

sentences.en: It's a way to kind of build a record of the past day by day.
sentences.zh: 所以我们仍在试图弄清楚这些组织方案可能是什么样子，

sentences.en: So we're still trying to figure out what those organizational schemes might look like,
sentences.zh: 但我很着迷于这种回溯一年的游戏实际上是我们交谈过的许多志愿者中普遍共有的事情。

sentences.en: but I'm fascinated that this game of going back a year is actually something that was commonly shared across a number of volunteers that we've spoken to.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，《华尔街日报》的一篇文章引用了你们俩的话，谈到了新冠疫情封锁是如何影响人们记忆的。

sentences.en: You were both quoted in a Wall Street Journal article last summer about how the COVID lockdowns were affecting people's memory.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And as you talked about this, going back a year, going back a year, and going back a year, what has the lockdown done to the memories of people with HSAM?
sentences.zh: 当您谈到这一点时，回溯一年、一年又一年，封锁对超忆症（HSAM）患者的记忆有什么影响？

sentences.en: So if you're directing this at me, I can tell you just in generalities.
sentences.zh: 如果您是问我，我只能从大体上告诉您。

sentences.en: And what we have heard from some of our volunteers is that they don't feel that their track record, their memory of the past is as good as it was.
sentences.zh: 我们从一些志愿者那里听到的是，他们觉得自己的记录，也就是对过去的记忆，不如以前那么好了。

sentences.en: Because there's not enough events and not enough things happening, not enough salient dates with real occurrences to be able to gravitate to.
sentences.zh: 因为没有足够的事件，没有足够多的事情发生，也没有足够多值得铭记的真实日期来作为锚点。

sentences.en: But we've heard the same thing also from everybody else.
sentences.zh: 但我们也从其他人那里听到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's just limited to HSAM.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这不仅仅局限于超忆症患者。

sentences.en: I think it really is kind of almost like a memory fog that we're all experiencing because it has been so monotonous and we've all been stuck at home and locked down.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这更像是一种我们都在经历的“记忆迷雾”，因为生活太单调了，我们都被困在家里，处于封锁状态。

sentences.en: And there hasn't been enough experiences with novelty in them that our memory systems kind of gravitate to and say, this is important.
sentences.zh: 而且生活中缺乏足够的新鲜体验，让我们的记忆系统能够捕捉并标记说：这很重要。

sentences.en: I need to store that for later use.
sentences.zh: 我需要把它存起来以后用。

sentences.en: But I'd love to hear from Marky what her feelings have been also.
sentences.zh: 但我很想听听Marky的感受。

sentences.en: Yeah, I would too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也想听听。

sentences.en: Is it disconcerting that you don't have these hooks to grab onto?
sentences.zh: 没有这些可以抓取的记忆钩子，会让人感到不安吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I've really found it's just a portion of lockdown.
sentences.zh: 我确实发现这只是封锁期间的一部分。

sentences.en: And maybe it's because I live in Alabama.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为我住在阿拉巴马州。

sentences.en: So it looks a little different here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的情况看起来有点不同。

sentences.en: But, you know, last March is really vivid.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，去年三月真的很生动。

sentences.en: Last March when, you know, I remember like, you know, everything shutting down and all of like how that was playing out.
sentences.zh: 去年三月，我记得一切是如何停摆的，以及事情是如何发展的。

sentences.en: And like my last, the last day, like the day we found out that like the university,
sentences.zh: 就像我最后的那一天，我们得知大学的那一天，

sentences.en: Auburn University was going to shut down like March 13th, right?
sentences.zh: 奥本大学要在3月13日关闭，对吧？

sentences.en: That was that Friday.
sentences.zh: 那是那个周五。

sentences.en: And then that Sunday on the 15th, all staff got an email like, hey, we're going to start doing some remote work.
sentences.zh: 然后到了15号周日，所有员工都收到了一封邮件，说我们要开始远程办公了。

sentences.en: And we're like, whoa, whoa, whoa, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，哇，哇，哇，发生什么事了？

sentences.en: And I remember, you know, on the 11th, that Wednesday, I was seeing the movie Emma about the Jane Austen novel.
sentences.zh: 我记得11号那天，周三，我正在看根据简·奥斯汀小说改编的电影《爱玛》。

sentences.en: And it was, you know, I didn't know it was the last time I'd be sitting in a movie theater for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不知道，那是我在很长一段时间内最后一次坐在电影院里了。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden my phone just starts buzzing and buzzing.
sentences.zh: 突然间，我的手机开始不停地响。

sentences.en: I was like, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，怎么了？

sentences.en: And the NBA is getting canceled.
sentences.zh: NBA要取消了。

sentences.en: March Madness is getting canceled.
sentences.zh: “疯狂三月”要取消了。

sentences.en: And it was like, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: But man, I have to tell you, April is blurry.
sentences.zh: 但伙计，我得告诉你，四月是一片模糊。

sentences.en: April is, is gone.
sentences.zh: 四月，已经消失了。

sentences.en: Like it's, I remember Easter, cause we did like a family Zoom Easter.
sentences.zh: 我只记得复活节，因为我们举行了家庭Zoom复活节聚会。

sentences.en: My boyfriend and I, and then my two friends that are back in Indiana.
sentences.zh: 我和我男朋友，还有我在印第安纳州的两个朋友。

sentences.en: We did, we played ticket to ride virtually together one weekend.
sentences.zh: 有一个周末我们一起在线玩了《车票之旅》。

sentences.en: And that'll be a year ago on this coming Sunday.
sentences.zh: 这个周日就满一年了。

sentences.en: So I remember that, but there's like very few events.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得那个，但除此之外几乎没有什么事件。

sentences.en: Because when you're working from home and you're not, and you're not even leaving your apartment, you know, for anything besides going to the grocery store, it's, it was murky.
sentences.zh: 因为当你居家办公，除了去杂货店之外甚至不出门时，一切都变得模糊不清。

sentences.en: But when it came back was Memorial Day weekend.
sentences.zh: 但到了阵亡将士纪念日周末，记忆又回来了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Memorial Day weekend of last year with not only having a holiday and things like that, but then the killing of George Floyd happened.
sentences.zh: 去年阵亡将士纪念日周末，不仅因为有假期，还因为乔治·弗洛伊德被杀事件发生了。

sentences.en: And so that is like, I think a big event for me that kind of like started the HCM again of like, okay, we're back, like, um, and events started happening.
sentences.zh: 所以我想那对我来说是一个重大事件，它重新启动了我的超忆症，让我觉得，好吧，我们回来了，事件开始发生了。

sentences.en: Dr. Yasser, what is the practical application of your work in this area?
sentences.zh: Yasser博士，您的研究在这个领域有什么实际应用吗？

sentences.en: I, I mentioned in the intro and looking at, at Alzheimer's kind of the opposite where people lose their autobiographical memory.
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中提到了阿尔茨海默病，这与人们失去自传体记忆的情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Is this going to help with that?
sentences.zh: 这会有所帮助吗？

sentences.en: We hope so.
sentences.zh: 我们希望如此。

sentences.en: And, um, in particular, some of our colleagues have also kind of identified what we think is,
sentences.zh: 特别是一些同事已经确定了我们认为的，

sentences.en: is the opposite scheme, uh, what would they call SDAM or severely deficient autobiographical memory.
sentences.zh: 相反的模式，也就是他们所说的SDAM，即严重缺陷自传体记忆。

sentences.en: So this is, uh, my colleague, Brian Levine and his laboratory, um, uh, have, uh, identified individuals who have very, very fuzzy records of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 这是我的同事Brian Levine和他的实验室发现的，他们确定了一些对过去记忆非常模糊的人。

sentences.en: Now they still do okay on other memory tests and okay in other facets of life.
sentences.zh: 他们在其他记忆测试和生活的其他方面表现尚可。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're not Alzheimer's patients or anything like that, but their record of the past is, uh, not as rich as, uh, uh, most of us, uh, would have.
sentences.zh: 他们不是阿尔茨海默病患者，但他们对过去的记录不像我们大多数人那样丰富。

sentences.en: So, so it seems like there is sort of a continuum or maybe a bell shaped curve with two extremes
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎是一个连续体，或者可能是一个有两个极端的钟形曲线，

sentences.en: here and understanding the extremes always informs us about the process and the mechanism.
sentences.zh: 了解极端情况总是能让我们洞察过程和机制。

sentences.en: When the condition, uh, was first identified, Dr.
sentences.zh: 当这个病症最初被发现时，McGaw博士，

sentences.en: McGaw, um, I think is quoted as, uh, saying this might, um, have us, you know, rewrite the textbooks and really rethink the way we think about memory.
sentences.zh: 我想他曾说过，这可能会让我们重写教科书，并真正重新思考我们对记忆的看法。

sentences.en: Cause we've always, you know, grown in the field to think that memory is adaptive because it, uh, doesn't store everything.
sentences.zh: 因为我们一直认为记忆是适应性的，因为它不会存储所有东西。

sentences.en: It leaves a lot out and really focuses on, um, things that can be used for generalizable knowledge.
sentences.zh: 它会遗漏很多细节，真正专注于那些可用于概括性知识的内容。

sentences.en: And in fact, um, there are lots of examples, um, about how damaging it would be if we tried to store everything because we would not be able to generalize.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有很多例子说明如果我们试图存储一切会有多大的破坏性，因为我们将无法进行概括。

sentences.en: However, seeing and, uh, uh, the experience of those with H-SAM suggests otherwise, suggest
sentences.zh: 然而，观察超忆症患者的经历表明情况并非如此，

sentences.en: that maybe we missed something in that original assessment and that it is possible to generalize
sentences.zh: 也许我们在最初的评估中遗漏了一些东西，即灵活地进行概括、应用知识并拥有卓越的过去记录是可能的。

sentences.en: flexibly and be able to apply knowledge and have an exceptional track record of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅从基础神经科学的角度来看，试图了解这种病症是非常有启发性的。

sentences.en: So at a, from a fundamental neuroscience perspective alone, it's really informative to try to understand that condition.
sentences.zh: 当然，一旦你了解了机器及其工作原理，你就可以开始了解它如何发生故障。

sentences.en: And of course, once you understand the machine and how it works, you can start to understand also how it breaks down.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这在记忆丧失的病症中会有很大的适用性，不仅是阿尔茨海默病，还有各种不同的神经精神疾病。

sentences.en: So I do think there's going to be a lot of, uh, applicability to conditions where we have memory loss, not just Alzheimer's disease, but a variety of different neuropsychiatric
sentences.zh: Marky，我猜由于你在Yas博士实验室的工作，你能够见到其他像你一样患有超忆症的人。

sentences.en: illnesses as well.
sentences.zh: 终于见到一个记忆力和你一样的人，是什么感觉？

sentences.en: So Marky, I'm guessing that as a result of your work with Dr. Yas's lab, that you were able to meet other people like yourself with H-SAM.

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.

sentences.en: Uh, so, uh, my, I bet I met Becky who is a lovely, lovely woman from Australia, um, from I believe, uh, Queensland, Australia, uh, that has H-SAM as well.

sentences.en: And her dream was to meet another person with H-SAM.

sentences.en: So they looked at kind of the prospective folks and noticed I was the closest one to her age and also a girl.

sentences.en: And so, um, you know, they thought it'd be good for us to meet.

sentences.en: So 60 Minutes and all their team flew my mom and I out to, uh, Los Angeles and, uh, we got

sentences.en: to meet Becky and, uh, they did this very dramatic, like walk-in scene of like me standing in a courtyard and like her walking in, like it was the bachelor or something.
sentences.zh: 所以我第一次见到她只有一次，但我必须表现得像第一次见到那样惊讶、震惊和敬畏。

sentences.en: Uh, and then also the hilarious part too, is like, and anyone listening to this who has filmed a TV show before will know this, but they had to do that take like 10 times.

sentences.en: And so I, you know, I, I met her for the first time once, but I had to act as like surprised and shocked and in awe as like I did the first time.
sentences.zh: 我们不是想出名什么的。

sentences.en: And, you know, Becky and I aren't TV actresses here.

sentences.en: Like we're not, we're not trying to get big or anything.

sentences.en: And we're like, okay.

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, it was kind of funny, uh, but Becky and I did get to develop a relationship and become friends.

sentences.en: And that was, that was the actual meaningful part.

sentences.en: And so it's really special when you get to meet Dr.

sentences.en: the extent of H Sam and be able to cater to different ranges of experiences and different ages, as Mark, you said.
